additional_requirements: manic_episode is present for the majority of the total duration of the active and residual portions of the illness
delusions_and_hallucinations occur for 2 or more weeks in the absence of a major mood episode

S019.name: Delusions
S019.description: Fixed beliefs that do not change easily, even in the face of contradictory evidence.

subtypes.Persecutory Delusions: The false belief that one is being harmed or monitored by other people or organizations.
subtypes.Referential Delusions: The conviction that ordinary events, remarks, or behaviors have specific relevance to oneself.
subtypes.Grandiose Delusions: The false belief that one possesses special abilities, power, or fame.
subtypes.Erotomanic Delusions: The false belief that another person is in love with or has affection for them.
subtypes.Nihilistic Delusions: A destructive or negative conviction that the world is ending or that a major catastrophe will occur.
subtypes.Somatic Delusions: The baseless conviction that there is a serious abnormality with one's body or organs.
subtypes.Jealous Delusions: The conviction that one's spouse or romantic partner is being unfaithful without sufficient evidence.

S020.name: Hallucinations
S020.description: Perception-like experiences that occur without an external stimulus and are as vivid and clear as normal perception.

subtypes.Auditory Hallucinations: The perceptual experience of hearing voices or sounds when there is no actual sound.
subtypes.Visual Hallucinations: The perceptual experience of seeing people or objects that do not exist.
subtypes.Tactile Hallucinations: Experiencing the sensation of being touched or movement on the skin when there is no actual stimulus.
subtypes.Olfactory Hallucinations: The perceptual experience of smelling odors that do not exist.
subtypes.Gustatory Hallucinations: The perceptual experience of tasting flavors that are not actually present.

S021.name: Disorganized_Thinking_Speech
S021.description: Symptoms where speech or thought appears scattered and difficult to follow due to a lack of logical or consistent flow.

subtypes.Derailment or Loose Associations: A speech pattern of switching rapidly from one topic to another with no logical connection between thoughts.
subtypes.Tangentiality: Speech that deviates entirely from the question and fails to answer directly.
subtypes.Incoherence or Word Salad: Severe fragmentation of speech and sentence structure, making it nearly impossible to understand.
subtypes.Neologisms: Using made-up words that have meaning only to the individual.
subtypes.Clang Associations: Speech governed by sounds, such as rhyming, rather than the meaning of words.

S024.name: Depressed_Mood
S024.description: A state where a sad, empty, or hopeless mood persists.

subtypes.Depressed Mood: A persistently sunken mood or feeling of depression.
subtypes.Tearfulness: A state of frequent crying or inability to hold back tears.
subtypes.Sadness: A state where a sad or gloomy mood is maintained continuously.
subtypes.Emptiness: A feeling of inner emptiness or a state of feeling no emotion.
subtypes.Emotional Numbness: A state where emotions feel dulled or paralyzed.

S025.name: Loss_of_Interest
S025.description: A state where interest or pleasure in previously enjoyed activities is markedly diminished.

subtypes.Loss of Interest: Reduced interest in previously enjoyed hobbies or leisure activities.
subtypes.Social Withdrawal: Reduced interest or effort in social interactions and maintaining relationships.
subtypes.Loss of Motivation: Lack of motivation to initiate or complete work or tasks.
subtypes.Anhedonia: Inability to experience positive emotions such as happiness, satisfaction, love, or pleasure.
subtypes.Indifference to Achievement: Insensitivity or indifference to personal achievements or success.

S026.name: Weight_Appetite_Change
S026.description: Significant increase or decrease in appetite or weight.

subtypes.Significant Weight Loss: Weight loss of more than 5% in a month without dieting.
subtypes.Weight Gain: Weight gain of more than 5% in a month.
subtypes.Decrease in Appetite: Decrease in appetite occurring nearly every day.
subtypes.Increase in Appetite: Increase in appetite occurring nearly every day.

S030.name: Worthlessness_Guilt
S030.description: Feelings of worthlessness or excessive or inappropriate guilt (which may be delusional; not merely self-reproach or guilt about being sick).

subtypes.Feelings of Worthlessness: The feeling that one is useless and has no value.
subtypes.Ruminative Guilt: A thought pattern of obsessively replaying past minor mistakes or flaws and constantly reproaching oneself.
subtypes.Excessive or Inappropriate Guilt: Feeling excessive responsibility for trivial matters or daily events and believing one deserves punishment.
subtypes.Delusional Guilt: Guilt reaching a delusional level, disconnected from reality, involving feeling responsible for unrelated unfortunate events.

S032.name: Death_Suicide
S032.description: Recurrent thoughts of death, recurrent suicidal ideation, or a suicide attempt.

subtypes.Recurrent Thoughts of Death: Passive wish to die (e.g., 'I wish I wouldn't wake up') without active intent to kill oneself.
subtypes.Suicidal Ideation: Recurring thoughts of 'I want to die' or 'I want to kill myself' without a specific plan.
subtypes.Suicidal Impulse: Strong, sudden urges to jump from a height or run into traffic without a concrete plan.
subtypes.Specific Plan for Suicide: Conceiving specific scenarios or methods regarding when, where, and how to die.
subtypes.Suicide Attempt: Actual actions taken to end one's life or preparatory behaviors like hoarding pills or writing a will.

S033.name: Elevated_Irritable_Mood
S033.description: A distinct period of abnormally and persistently elevated, expansive, or irritable mood.

subtypes.Elevated Mood: A mood that is abnormally high, euphoric, and full of unmotivated happiness and vitality.
subtypes.Irritable Mood: A state where one gets angry or aggressive even at minor stimuli.
subtypes.Mood Lability: Rapid shifts in mood, alternating unpredictably between euphoria and irritability.

S034.name: Increased_Activity
S034.description: Abnormally and persistently increased goal-directed activity or energy.

subtypes.Increased Energy: Overflowing physical and mental energy, leading to an inability to stay still and a desire to keep moving.
subtypes.Hyperactivity: Doing far more work than usual or starting multiple activities simultaneously.
subtypes.Psychomotor Agitation: Inability to tolerate resting or stopping, driven by a constant need to do something.

S035.name: Inflated_Self_Esteem
S035.description: Inflated self-esteem or grandiosity (may range from uncritical self-confidence to delusional proportions).

subtypes.Inflated Self-Confidence: Feeling capable of anything and believing that failure is impossible, unlike one's usual self.
subtypes.Overestimation of Abilities: Unrealistically assessing one's talents, knowledge, or abilities as superior.
subtypes.Grandiose Delusions: The false belief that one is a special and important person with a special mission or purpose.

S036.name: Decreased_Sleep
S036.description: Decreased need for sleep (e.g., feels rested after only 3 hours of sleep).

subtypes.Reduced Sleep Duration: Sleeping significantly less than usual but feeling refreshed rather than tired.
subtypes.Loss of Sleep Need: Not feeling the urge to sleep or the thought that sleep is necessary.
subtypes.Indifference to Insomnia: Feeling no problem and continuing activities despite staying up for several nights.

S038.name: Racing_Thoughts
S038.description: Flight of ideas or subjective experience that thoughts are racing.

subtypes.Racing Thoughts: Thoughts spinning too fast in the head, constantly jumping from one idea to another.
subtypes.Flooding of Thoughts: Too many thoughts emerging simultaneously, making them disorganized.
subtypes.Inability to Control Thoughts: Unable to stop or slow down thoughts and unable to calm the mind.

S039.name: Manic_Distractibility
S039.description: Attention is too easily drawn to unimportant or irrelevant external stimuli.

subtypes.Responsiveness to Extraneous Stimuli: Attention is immediately drawn to trivial and unimportant stimuli nearby (e.g., noise, movement).
subtypes.Frequent Task Switching: Unable to finish one task and constantly shifting attention to new things, starting multiple tasks simultaneously.
subtypes.Inability to Sustain Attention: Unable to focus on any activity for long, with attention constantly being scattered.

S040.name: Increased_Goal_Activity
S040.description: Increase in goal-directed activity (at work, school, socially, or sexually) or purposeless psychomotor agitation.

subtypes.Occupational Hyperactivity: Driving significantly more projects or work than usual in the workplace or academic setting.
subtypes.Social Hyperactivity: Becoming much more sociable and extroverted than usual, actively meeting and contacting people.
subtypes.Hypersexuality: Significantly increased interest in or activity regarding sex.
subtypes.Psychomotor Agitation: Purposeless non-goal-directed activity, such as pacing or hand-wringing, driven by an inability to sit still.

symptom.disease_info: Schizoaffective Disorder (Bipolar Type) is characterized by a combination of psychotic symptoms (such as delusions and hallucinations) and mood episodes meeting full criteria for mania, with or without major depressive episodes, where psychotic symptoms also occur for at least two weeks in the absence of prominent mood symptoms. The course is typically chronic or episodic with periods of partial remission, and functional impairment is common in social and occupational domains. It is distinguished from bipolar disorder with psychotic features by the presence of psychosis outside of mood episodes, and from schizophrenia by the prominence and duration of mood episodes over the illness course. Onset is often in late adolescence or early adulthood but can emerge later in the context of psychosocial stressors, substance use, or medical comorbidity, especially in individuals with a pre-existing vulnerability.

patient.personality: A curious, creative young man who combines meticulous work with spontaneous artistic pursuits, balancing structured budgeting habits with occasional impulsive indulgence in art and music.
patient.stressor: Brian’s problems emerged toward the end of his first year working as an accounting clerk, when long-standing tensions at home escalated after his parents’ separation and his father’s abrupt move out of state. Trying to help his mother manage finances while working full-time, he initially threw himself into both responsibilities, spending late nights perfecting reports and then sketching or going to shows to blow off steam, feeling unusually driven and confident about fixing everything. Over time, the strain of shifting family roles, unresolved anger toward his father, and his own high expectations led to increasingly erratic cycles of intense productivity and withdrawal, and his once-enjoyable solitary activities like hiking and journaling began to be overshadowed by bleak ruminations about failure and the pointlessness of his efforts. Over the next 2 years and 5 months, his functioning at work and in his volunteer tutoring declined, he became socially isolated, and his thoughts about death grew more frequent and detailed, culminating in him seeking psychiatric help after confiding to a close friend that he had started planning ways to end his life.
patient.chief_complaint: “I’ve been thinking a lot about dying lately, and it’s getting to the point where I’m scared of what I might do.”

S019.name: Delusions
S019.description: Fixed beliefs that do not change easily, even in the face of contradictory evidence.
S019.manifestation: For a long time now I’ve been convinced that my dad leaving wasn’t just a divorce thing, that he and my old boss are somehow working together behind the scenes to test me or ruin my reputation, like the mistakes in my spreadsheets or random comments from coworkers are all part of some plan aimed at me personally, no matter how many times people tell me that’s impossible.

S020.name: Hallucinations
S020.description: Perception-like experiences that occur without an external stimulus and are as vivid and clear as normal perception.
S020.manifestation: When I’m alone at my desk or lying in bed, I hear this male voice, kind of like my own but harsher, talking over my thoughts, telling me I’m a fraud and that everyone at work and at home can see it, and sometimes it even whispers exact phrases my manager later says in meetings, which makes it feel even more real and terrifying.

S021.name: Disorganized_Thinking_Speech
S021.description: Symptoms where speech or thought appears scattered and difficult to follow due to a lack of logical or consistent flow.
S021.manifestation: When I try to explain what’s going on, my words just go all over the place—I'll start talking about a late invoice and suddenly jump to my dad’s new girlfriend and then to some song lyric that’s stuck in my head, and by the time I stop, people are just staring at me like they have no idea what I’m talking about, and honestly neither do I.

S024.name: Depressed_Mood
S024.description: A state where a sad, empty, or hopeless mood persists.
S024.manifestation: Most days now I wake up with this heavy, sinking feeling, like there’s no point in getting out of bed or going to the office because nothing I do matters and I’m just watching my life slowly fall apart from the inside.

S025.name: Loss_of_Interest
S025.description: A state where interest or pleasure in previously enjoyed activities is markedly diminished.
S025.manifestation: I used to love hiking on weekends and staying up sketching album covers in my notebook, but lately even the thought of picking up a pencil or putting on my boots feels pointless and exhausting, so I just sit there scrolling on my phone or staring at the wall instead of doing anything I used to care about.

S026.name: Weight_Appetite_Change
S026.description: Significant increase or decrease in appetite or weight.
S026.manifestation: My eating has been all over the place—during the really low stretches I’ll go an entire day at my desk with just coffee because I feel too numb or guilty to bother with food, and then when I get wound up and wired I’ll suddenly down a whole pizza at midnight without even really tasting it, and my weight’s been jumping up and down because of it.

S030.name: Worthlessness_Guilt
S030.description: Feelings of worthlessness or excessive or inappropriate guilt (which may be delusional; not merely self-reproach or guilt about being sick).
S030.manifestation: I keep replaying every small mistake I’ve ever made—like misplacing a receipt at work or snapping at my mom—and twisting it into this belief that I’m the reason our family fell apart and that I should be punished for wrecking everyone’s lives, even though people tell me that doesn’t make sense.

S032.name: Death_Suicide
S032.description: Recurrent thoughts of death, recurrent suicidal ideation, or a suicide attempt.
S032.manifestation: For months I’ve had these detailed thoughts about dying, like picturing myself stepping off the bridge on my walk home or lining up my mom’s sleeping pills in a certain order, and even when I’m not actively planning it, I catch myself wishing I wouldn’t wake up the next day because it feels like that would be easier for everyone.

S033.name: Elevated_Irritable_Mood
S033.description: A distinct period of abnormally and persistently elevated, expansive, or irritable mood.
S033.manifestation: I go through these stretches where I feel oddly invincible and on edge at the same time—like I’m buzzing, talking fast, cracking jokes at work, and staying out all night at shows, but then the tiniest thing, like my mom asking about a bill, sets me off and I snap at her or slam doors for no real reason.

S034.name: Increased_Activity
S034.description: Abnormally and persistently increased goal-directed activity or energy.
S034.manifestation: On my high days I can’t sit still at all—I’ll clean the whole apartment, reorganize my mom’s files, start three new budgeting spreadsheets for fun, and then decide at 2 a.m. that I absolutely have to redesign my entire sketch portfolio, all while pacing around like I’m plugged into an outlet.

S035.name: Inflated_Self_Esteem
S035.description: Inflated self-esteem or grandiosity (may range from uncritical self-confidence to delusional proportions).
S035.manifestation: There are times when I’m so revved up that I honestly believe I’m some kind of financial genius-artist hybrid, like I’m going to revolutionize accounting software and music visuals at the same time, and I’ll tell people I’m destined to fix my family’s money problems and make us rich, even though I’m just an accounting clerk who barely passed high school math.

S036.name: Decreased_Sleep
S036.description: Decreased need for sleep (e.g., feels rested after only 3 hours of sleep).
S036.manifestation: When I get into those wired phases, I’ll sleep maybe two or three hours a night, if that, and still feel totally charged, like my brain is too busy planning projects and connecting ideas to bother with something as boring and unnecessary as sleep.

S038.name: Racing_Thoughts
S038.description: Flight of ideas or subjective experience that thoughts are racing.
S038.manifestation: My thoughts start racing so fast that it feels like a radio stuck between stations—numbers from work, memories of my dad leaving, new song ideas, random worries about the future all blasting at once—so I can’t grab onto a single thought long enough to finish a sentence or fill out a simple form.

S039.name: Manic_Distractibility
S039.description: Attention is too easily drawn to unimportant or irrelevant external stimuli.
S039.manifestation: When I’m in that amped-up mode, my attention bounces off everything—the clicking pens in the office, someone walking past the door, a color pattern on a spreadsheet—and I’ll abandon what I’m supposed to be doing to chase those little distractions until I have four half-finished tasks and nothing actually completed.

S040.name: Increased_Goal_Activity
S040.description: Increase in goal-directed activity (at work, school, socially, or sexually) or purposeless psychomotor agitation.
S040.manifestation: In those intense bursts I suddenly decide I’m going to fix all our finances, ace my job, launch an art page, and reconnect with every friend I’ve ever had, so I start emailing my boss new ideas, drawing logo drafts, rearranging my mom’s bills, and messaging people nonstop, pacing around the house like I’m preparing for some huge mission I can’t slow down from.
